title: Initial values and later model changes
summary: Model initialization, default fallback, and changed model input behavior.

facts.claim: For an application-computed initial value available before field build, initialize the model; the official demo prefers model initialization.
conditions: The initial value is available before the relevant field build.
limits: The demo does not prescribe a hook or an asynchronous update strategy.
facts.context: Choosing where a computed initial field value belongs.
facts.source_quote:
The official default-value demo presents initializing the model as the preferred
choice and field `defaultValue` as the other choice. Its `lastName` model value
is present while the field also has a `defaultValue`; the field's `firstName`
uses `defaultValue` with no initial model value [E14a](sources.md#e14a),
[E14b](sources.md#e14b).

facts.claim: A field defaultValue fills an undefined keyed model value when the field is eligible; it does not overwrite an already supplied model value.
limits: Hidden fields have separate build conditions.
facts.context: Why an initial model value takes precedence over a field default.
facts.source_quote:
Core assigns a field's `defaultValue` only when the keyed model value is
undefined and the field is not hidden under the relevant build conditions.
An application-computed initial value can therefore be placed in the model
before that field is built; `defaultValue` is the undefined-value fallback,
not an override of an existing model value [K05](sources.md#k05).

facts.claim: A qualifying changed model input can trigger a FormlyForm rebuild.
conditions: The changed input passes the component change condition.
limits: This does not show that defaultValue reacts to arbitrary later state changes or that a field hook is required.
facts.context: Supplying a later-computed value through the application model.
facts.source_quote:
For a value arriving after the initial build, the Formly form component accepts
a model input and can rebuild when Angular reports a changed model input that
passes its change check. This supports supplying a changed model from
application state; it does not establish
that a field `defaultValue` watches later state or that a hook is required
[K11](sources.md#k11). The consuming app still needs to check timing and
reference-change behavior.
